title: AFIR and ISO 15118-20: what changes for chargers installed from 2027
description: From 1 January 2027 newly installed AC charging points in the EU must support ISO 15118-20. What that means for owners, installers and existing chargers.
markdown:
From 1 January 2027, AC charging points that are newly installed or renovated in the EU must support ISO 15118-20. The rule comes from a delegated regulation under AFIR, the EU's Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation, and it covers public and private charging points.

## What ISO 15118 is

ISO 15118 is the language a car and a charger use to talk to each other over the charging cable. Today most AC chargers only tell the car how much current it may draw. With ISO 15118 the two can exchange much more: who the driver is, how much energy the car needs and by when, and, in the newest version, energy flowing back from the car.

## What you get from it

- **Plug & Charge.** The car identifies itself when it is plugged in. No app and no card.
- **Smarter charging.** The charger knows the car's needs and can plan around prices and the building's load.
- **Bidirectional charging.** ISO 15118-20 is the basis for sending energy from the car back to the building or the grid.

## What changes, and for whom

- **You are installing chargers in 2027 or later:** the charger must support ISO 15118-20.
- **You already have chargers:** nothing changes. The rule applies to new installations and renovations.
- **You run public charging:** ad hoc payment and showing the price before charging are already required. For AC chargers a QR code payment page is enough.

## What VOOL is doing

The new VOOL Charger supports ISO 15118-2, ISO 15118-20 and Plug & Charge, and ships from mid-December 2026. Bidirectional charging follows as a firmware update in the first quarter of 2027. Existing VOOL chargers can be upgraded by swapping the charge controller; the casing and cabling stay.
